sections.h2: Urbandale and the Polk-Dallas county line
sections.html:
Northwest of downtown Des Moines, Urbandale spreads across two counties, Polk and Dallas. Your property tax bill comes from whichever county holds your parcel.

The city covers about 22.5 square miles where Interstates 35 and 80 meet, along Iowa Highway 141, and U.S. Route 6 forms its southern border with Clive. The 2020 census counted 45,580 people, twelfth among Iowa cities, and the median age was 39.3.

sections.h2: A streetcar suburb that grew after 1950
sections.html:
Urbandale incorporated on April 16, 1917, as a streetcar suburb of Des Moines. Streetcar service ended in 1951, and many DART bus routes now follow the old streetcar paths. Growth was fast after that:

  • 1920: 298 residents
  • 1950: 1,777 residents
  • 1970: 14,434 residents
  • 2000: 29,072 residents
  • 2020: 45,580 residents

Most of the growth came after 1950, so much of the housing is postwar. Owners are more likely to be dealing with mid-century or later systems than with century-old ones.

sections.h2: Home values and who lives here
sections.html:
Urbandale is a high-income, mostly owner-occupied suburb. For 2020 to 2024 the owner-occupied rate is 78.1 percent and the median value of owner-occupied homes is $335,500. Median household income is $112,795, median gross rent is $1,211 and households average 2.64 people.

With values that high, a house that needs a new roof or kitchen shows a wide gap between asking price and condition, which is a common reason owners weigh an as-is sale. Finance and insurance lead the local economy at 17.9 percent of employment, followed by health care and social assistance at 11.8 percent, and Marsh and McLennan Companies is the largest named employer.

Snowfall averages 36.5 inches a season, and storms are part of the record: an F2 tornado hit on October 16, 1966, and an EF1 tornado on July 15, 2024. If you are selling, the practical checklist is short:

  • Roof age and any hail or wind repair history.
  • Furnace and air conditioner age.
  • Basement moisture after heavy spring rain.

An insurance claim in the last few years may need to be explained to a buyer, so keep the paperwork.

sections.h2: Which school district is the house in?
sections.html:
The Urbandale Community School District runs six elementary schools, one middle school and Urbandale High School. Parts of the city are also served by the Dallas Center-Grimes, Des Moines, Johnston, Waukee and West Des Moines districts. Two neighbors a block apart may attend different districts.

Buyers and agents ask about this early, so confirm your attendance district before you describe the property. Private options include Des Moines Christian School and St. Pius X Catholic School.

The city maintains 850 acres of parks and 54 miles of recreational trails that connect to other Des Moines-area trails. DART Route 74 serves the northwestern business areas and connects to Windsor Heights and Valley West Mall, and business parks along the Urban Loop put many workplaces close to home. Mention park and trail access if your house is near one. Short drives to the interstates are another selling point for commuters.

Living History Farms is the best-known landmark, and the Olmsted Family Farmhouse, built in 1904, is the city's only site on the National Register of Historic Places.

In general the city wants a building permit for any construction, with separate permits for plumbing, mechanical and electrical work. A portable shed still needs zoning approval and has to stay clear of easements. Apply through the city's online system or at Community Development, 3600 86th Street. Building services is at 515-278-3935.

Fees in the schedule effective July 1, 2026:

Permit or violationFee
Fence permit$30
Furnace or heater (mechanical)$15 per unit
Water heater (mechanical)$7 per unit
Work done without a permitDouble fee, building capped at $750
Tall weeds$50 admin fee plus mowing cost
Municipal infraction$750 first, $1,000 repeat

If past owners finished a basement or swapped a furnace without a permit, a buyer's inspector may ask about it, and sorting that out before closing can take time.

sections.h2: Property tax, transfer tax and disclosure
sections.html:
Dallas County splits the tax bill into September 1 and March 1 payments. Each goes delinquent after September 30 and March 31 respectively, and interest then runs at 1.5 percent a month. The Dallas County Treasurer is in Adel at 800 Court Street, Suite 111. If your house is on the Polk County side, call the Polk County Treasurer for its schedule.

Transfer tax is 80 cents for each $500 of value past the first $500. A declaration of value travels with the deed to the county recorder, filed by the closing agent. The seller's written disclosure under Iowa Code 558A.4 reaches items like significant structural defects and lead service lines.

sections.h2: What to bring to a sale conversation
sections.html:
Pull together the deed, your most recent property tax statement, mortgage payoff information and any permit paperwork for past work. If a furnace, water heater or finished basement was added by a prior owner, say so, and note whether a permit exists. If the roof or siding was repaired after a storm, keep the claim file and invoices with the rest.

It also helps to know who your neighbors are in the district sense: confirm the school district, the county that bills your tax and whether any city notices are open on the lot, such as tall weeds or a fence issue. None of that blocks a cash sale, but open items are cheaper to settle when you know about them up front.

sections.h2: Ways to sell an Urbandale house
sections.html:
• Agent listing: suits a house in good shape that can wait out showings and a buyer's loan.
  • Sale by owner: skips commission but leaves disclosure and negotiation to you.
  • Cash sale: quicker, with no repairs, a fit for inherited, tenant-occupied or storm-damaged homes.

Collect two written offers or plans and compare net proceeds, closing dates and contingencies.

You describe the house and its condition, and we make an offer after reviewing it and the title. If you accept, a title company confirms ownership, requests payoff letters for any mortgage and prepares the deed. You choose the closing date, sign, and receive what is left after liens and unpaid taxes.

Because the city and two counties are involved, tell us early which county your parcel is in, whether any permits were left open, and whether a basement or mechanical upgrade was done without one. That lets the closing agent chase the right records instead of discovering gaps late.

faqs.q: Which county do I pay property tax to in Urbandale?
faqs.a: It depends on your parcel, since Urbandale lies in both Polk and Dallas counties. Check your tax statement. Dallas County's dates are September 1 and March 1.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a furnace or water heater in Urbandale?
faqs.a: Mechanical work needs a separate permit. The 2026 schedule lists $15 for a furnace or heater and $7 for a water heater, with a double fee for unpermitted work.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Urbandale?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $335,500 for 2020 to 2024. Your own value varies with age, size and condition.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Urbandale house that has storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes, as-is. Keep any insurance claim records. Urbandale had an EF1 tornado on July 15, 2024.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Urbandale house in?
faqs.a: The Urbandale Community School District is the main one, but parts of the city belong to Dallas Center-Grimes, Des Moines, Johnston, Waukee or West Des Moines. Confirm your address with the district.
